The directory name is the command, and `src/<command>.ts` implements it. Both
halves are checked: a page for a command nobody wrote and a command whose page
was never written are the two ways this tree can lie about what the tool does.

Every page carries the same shape — the invocation as its heading, a `## Usage`
block listing every flag, then the reasoning. The flag list is the one part
duplicated from `src/cli.ts`, and it is duplicated on purpose: a reader looking
up a command should not have to read the parser.

## Structure

    [command]/
      README.MD  the page for one command

Zero or more `[command]/` directories may exist. For each one that does,
README.MD is required. Nothing else may exist under docs/cli/.

## Not described here

    AGENTS.MD  Written by `espalier build` from the rules above.

Nothing above describes these, so nothing here tells you how to write them. That makes them a poor place to put work that belongs in the list above: a file with nowhere legal to go is a gap to report, not one to route around.

## docs/cli/[command]/README.MD — the page for one command

One directory per command, named for the command, holding
a `README.MD` that opens with the invocation as its heading and carries a
`## Usage` block showing every flag.

The command must exist: `src/<command>.ts` implements it. A page for a command
nobody wrote, or a command whose page was never written, are the two ways this
tree lies about what the tool does.
